title: Customer Protection – Limiting Liability in Unauthorized Electronic Banking Transactions
summary: Mandates zero customer liability when unauthorized transaction occurs due to contributory fraud/negligence/deficiency on the part of the bank, or third-party breach reported within 3 working days.
key_clauses: Zero Liability: Customer notifies the bank within 3 working days of receiving communication from the bank regarding unauthorized transaction.
Limited Liability: Customer notifies between 4 to 7 working days; maximum liability capped at ₹5,000 for basic savings/credit cards with limit ≤ ₹5 lakh, and ₹10,000 for other accounts.
Beyond 7 working days: Customer liability is determined as per the board-approved policy of the bank.
Burden of Proof: The burden of proving customer liability in unauthorized electronic banking transactions lies entirely upon the bank.
Reversal Timeline: Bank must credit the shadow reversal value to customer account within 10 working days of notification.

title: Framework for Tokenisation and Card-on-File Storage
summary: Prohibits merchants and payment aggregators from storing actual card numbers (PAN), expiry dates, or CVV; requires device-specific or merchant-specific tokenization.
key_clauses: No entity in the card transaction flow other than card issuers and card networks shall store actual card data (CoF).
Explicit customer consent with Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA) required for token registration.
Tokens must be cryptographically bound to specific merchant and consumer device to prevent cross-site fraud.

title: NPCI Guidelines on UPI Daily Limits and P2M Interchange
summary: Standardizes standard daily limit for standard UPI peer-to-peer (P2P) transfers to ₹1,00,000 per day, with elevated limits of ₹5,00,000 for capital markets, insurance, and medical/educational institutions.
key_clauses: Standard UPI P2P daily transaction cap: ₹1,00,000 across all UPI applications.
Higher educational institutions and healthcare emergency payments cap: ₹5,00,000 per transaction.
Mandatory 4-digit or 6-digit MPIN for every outgoing debit authorization; no pre-authorized debits without e-mandate registration.

title: Fair Lending Practice – Penal Charges in Loan Accounts and Transparent Recovery
summary: Regulates penal interest charges on loan default: penalty must be levied strictly as 'penal charges' and not compounded as 'penal interest' added to principal.
key_clauses: Penalty for non-compliance of loan terms must be treated as reasonable penal charges, not additional rate of interest.
No capitalization of penal charges (no interest computed on penal charges).
Lenders must provide clear disclosure of quantum and reason for penal charges in the loan agreement and key facts statement.
